title: Dedup Sorted
statement: Implement `solve(items)`. `items` is sorted ascending. Remove adjacent duplicates. Return `[length, prefix]` where `prefix` holds the unique values in order. Non-adjacent logic is unnecessary because equals are already adjacent.
constraints: Keep the first copy of each run
hints: The first element always stays, when the list is non-empty.
Copy an element only when it differs from the last kept value.
The length is the length of that prefix. An empty input returns [0, []].

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: On a sorted array, uniqueness is a comparison with the previous kept value.

editorial: On a sorted array, uniqueness is a comparison with the previous kept value. A set would also work and would spend extra memory and lose the reason the input was sorted. The write index is the classic in-place form.
